threads.label: Talk Tennis
threads.title: Jack Draper ends season early.
threads.body: Former world number four Jack Draper has decided not to play again this season. He has suffered from bone bruising on his serving arm for over a year. He had tried changing his serve and strings and diet, but no one seems to know the root cause of the problem. He has only played nine events since Wimbledon 2025. Can Draper come back from this?

threads.title: Most important body skills for serve
threads.body: List the top 3 body skills needed for the serve, in descending order. This is not about the technique of toss and swing. This is about fundamental body skills which are needed to implement the technique. Knowing this, one will be more aware of what exactly is lacking instead of trying out an endless number of technique tips. An example might be: ability to separate the movement of tossing and hitting arms.

threads.title: Lock out tension vs constant pull with different strings
threads.body: Hi, I've recently bought a Gamma Momentum ST and I've been stringing my rackets with poly strings at 52 lbs on this machine. On the RacquetTune App, I'm getting a reading of about 44 lbs. This is the same reading I got when the shop would string with a constant pull at 48 lbs. So in my mind, 48 lbs on a constant pull = 52 lbs on a lock-out machine (8% increase). I'll add that when I play with the racket I strung, it feels very similar to how it felt when the shop strung it. I'm very picky... Read more

threads.title: Zverev's 2 slam year validates Djokovic's 2025 slam level.
threads.body: Recall that Djokovic made 4 SFs in 2025 including a 4 set QF victory over current RG and US Open champ Zverev. Djokovic won the last 3 sets 6-3 6-2 6-4, making Zverev look like one dimensional chump. It's simply further validation of Djokovic's incredible slam level in 2025, not far from his 21-23 level, which was enough to convincingly beat a multi-slam winner. It's just too bad it wasn't enough to beat ATGs.
